name: Ninja (Tyler Blevins)
bio: Richard Tyler Blevins, better known by his online gaming alias Ninja, is an American professional esports player and livestreamer. Starting his competitive career in Halo 3, he exploded to unprecedented mainstream prominence during the rapid rise of Fortnite Battle Royale in 2018. Ninja shattered Twitch viewership records, appeared on the cover of ESPN The Magazine, and brought livestreaming culture into household conversation.

famousWorks.title: Record-breaking Fortnite Twitch stream with Drake and Travis Scott (628k concurrent viewers)
First professional esports gamer on the cover of ESPN The Magazine
Release of official Fortnite in-game Ninja Icon Series skin

awards: Streamy Award for Creator of the Year (2018)
The Game Awards Content Creator of the Year (2018)

faq.q: What record did Ninja break on Twitch in March 2018?
faq.a: He broke the record for the most-watched non-tournament Twitch stream with 628,000 concurrent viewers while playing Fortnite with musician Drake.

faq.q: What esports games did Ninja compete in professionally before Fortnite?
faq.a: He competed professionally in Halo 3, Halo: Reach, Halo 4, and H1Z1 before transitioning to Fortnite.

name: Faker (Lee Sang-hyeok)
bio: Lee Sang-hyeok, known by his legendary gamer tag Faker, is a South Korean professional League of Legends player for T1. Universally heralded as the undisputed greatest esports player of all time ('the GOAT'), he has achieved a record four League of Legends World Championships (2013, 2015, 2016, and 2023). Faker became the inaugural inductee into Riot Games' League of Legends Hall of Legends in 2024.

famousWorks.title: First World Championship title with SK Telecom T1 & famous Zed mirror-match outplay
Second World Championship title with a near-flawless 15–1 tournament run
Third World Championship title and Finals MVP honors
Historic fourth World Championship victory in Seoul, cementing his GOAT status
Inaugural inductee into the League of Legends Hall of Legends

awards: 4 League of Legends World Championship Titles (2013, 2015, 2016, 2023)
Inaugural Inductee - League of Legends Hall of Legends (2024)
Asian Games Gold Medalist for South Korea (Hangzhou 2022)
The Game Awards Best Esports Athlete (2017, 2023)

faq.q: Why is Faker called 'The Unkillable Demon King'?
faq.a: He earned the nickname from opponents and casters because of his near-supernatural mechanical reflexes, dodges, and champion mastery that make him virtually impossible to kill in lane.

faq.q: Has Faker ever played for another esports team?
faq.a: No, Faker has remained loyal to the T1 organization (formerly SK Telecom T1) throughout his entire professional career since 2013.
